variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
x = 10
const PI_VAL = 3.14159

# Type annotation (optional)
y::Float64 = 20.5
variables.notes: Variables are dynamically typed by default. `const` declares a constant (for performance in global scope).

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
i = 42        # Int64
f = 3.14      # Float64
c = 1 + 2im   # Complex
r = 3 // 4    # Rational
b = true      # Bool
s = "string"  # String
data_types.notes: Julia has a rich type system designed for numerical computing.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
2 + 3 * 4
2^10        # Exponentiation
7 % 3       # Remainder
7 ÷ 3       # Integer division

# Dot syntax for broadcasting element-wise
[1, 2, 3] .^ 2
operators.notes: Broadcasting with the dot operator `.` is heavily used in Julia for element-wise operations.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if x > 0
    println("Positive")
elseif x < 0
    println("Negative")
else
    println("Zero")
end

# Ternary operator
res = x > 0 ? "Pos" : "Neg"

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
for i in 1:10
    println(i^2)
end

# Array comprehension
squares = [i^2 for i in 1:10]
for_loop.notes: Iterates over a range. Array comprehensions are concise and fast.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
count = 0
while count < 5
    println(count)
    global count += 1 # global needed if in global scope
end
while_loop.notes: Loops require `global` when modifying global variables due to scoping rules.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Functions support multiple dispatch based on argument types.

arrays.title: Arrays & Matrices
arrays.code:
vec = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
mat = [1 2 3; 4 5 6]

# Accessing (1-based indexing)
val = mat[1, 2]

# Slicing
col = mat[:, 2]
arrays.notes: Julia arrays are 1-based and column-major order.

maps.title: Dictionaries
maps.code:
dict = Dict("a" => 1, "b" => 2)

# Accessing
val = dict["a"]

# Adding a key-value pair
dict["c"] = 3
maps.notes: Dictionaries use the `Dict` type with `=>` to define pairs.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
try
    result = 1 / 0
catch e
    if isa(e, DivideError)
        println("Cannot divide by zero")
    else
        println("An error occurred: ", e)
    end
finally
    println("Cleanup")
end
error_handling.notes: try-catch-finally block. Errors can be type-checked.

comments.title: Comments & Headers
comments.code:
# Comment in Julia
# Multi-line comments or docstrings
# are documented here
comments.notes: Julia uses # or language-specific delimiters (% in MATLAB, ! in Fortran) for comments.

numbers.title: Vectors, Matrices & Numbers
numbers.notes: Julia is optimized for vector and matrix calculations with high-precision numerical representations.

booleans.title: Logical Vectors & Booleans
booleans.code:
is_valid = TRUE
flags = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
booleans.notes: Julia provides boolean types with support for element-wise vector logic operations.

type_casting.title: Type Coercion & Casting
type_casting.notes: Julia converts data between numeric, character, factor, and logical representations.

strings.title: Strings & Character Vectors
strings.notes: Julia treats strings as atomic character scalars or vector arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Julia formats numerical output with sprintf formatting specifiers.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Switches
pattern_matching.notes: Julia executes branch logic via switch, ifelse, or conditional filtering.

range.title: Sequences & Indexing
range.notes: Julia indexes matrices and vectors using 1-based indexing and sequence generators.

iterators.title: Vectorized Apply & Iteration
iterators.notes: Julia emphasizes vectorized functional processing (apply, map) over explicit loops.

oop_classes.title: Object Systems & S3/S4
oop_classes.code:
# Object systems in Julia
obj = list(name = "Model", score = 0.95)
class(obj) = "metric"
oop_classes.notes: Julia uses class dispatch systems (S3/S4 in R, multiple dispatch in Julia) for data modeling.

lists.title: DataFrames & Lists
lists.notes: Julia stores heterogeneous columnar records in data frames and lists.

tuples.title: Pairs & Records
tuples.notes: Julia uses named vectors or lightweight structures for data records.

sets.title: Set Operations
sets.notes: Julia provides native mathematical set functions (union, intersect, setdiff).

modules_import.title: Libraries & Packages
modules_import.notes: Julia loads package namespaces using library or import declarations.
